items.title: GPG Encryptor
items.tagline: A point-and-click Tkinter GUI for encrypting and decrypting files and folders with GPG.
items.problem: Encrypting and decrypting files with GPG from the command line is error-prone for routine, repeated tasks like backups and one-off file sharing.
items.approach: Built a desktop GUI on top of GPG supporting recipient, password, and tar-password encryption modes, plus matching decrypt and tar-restore workflows, with dry-run previews and progress tracking. Packaged for one-command installation via pipx with a native desktop launcher.
items.outcome: A self-contained Linux desktop app installable with a single script, giving GPG encryption a proper GUI instead of remembering flag combinations.
items.lessons: Wrapping a well-understood CLI tool in a GUI is mostly about surfacing the right defaults and safety nets (dry runs, overwrite checks) rather than reinventing the underlying tool.

items.title: AD&D Character Generator
items.tagline: A character generator that follows the AD&D player book setup process.
items.problem: Manual AD&D character setup can be slow and repetitive, especially for new players who are still learning the process.
items.approach: Built a guided generator based on the AD&D player book flow, originally to make character creation easier and more engaging for my son.
items.outcome: A usable early version that mirrors core AD&D character creation steps while making the process faster and easier to follow.
items.lessons: Mapping tabletop rules into software works best when each step is explicit, validated, and easy to revisit.

items.title: Sams C++ 2005 Source Code
items.tagline: A student resource with extracted C++ examples organized by chapter.
items.problem: Working through a textbook is easier when code examples are available as separate files instead of embedded in long chapter text.
items.approach: Used a small extraction script to iterate through chapter material and split example code into individual .cpp files, organized by chapter for quick access.
items.outcome: A structured repository students can browse by chapter to find, compile, and experiment with the examples more easily.
items.lessons: Turning reference material into a learning resource often comes down to practical organization and fast lookup, not complex tooling.
